title: wt restore <dir> --json
description: What `wt restore <dir>` did. Printed by `wt restore <dir> --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Locations, the branch and the steps are read from the quarantine when the object is written. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

outcome.description: restored: the worktree is registered at its path again, with the branch action done, the quarantine's lock is off and its pins are deleted. refused: nothing changed. partial: a step failed after others were done; recovery.json says which, and wt restore <dir> again finishes it. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

unlocked.description: This run took the quarantine's lock off.

steps.description: The restore's steps as recovery.json records them — branch, moveAdmin, relink, moveCheckout, unlock, unpin — or empty when it has none. The list is closed.

location.description: original: at path, the same directory (by inode) — moved back, or never moved. quarantined: in the quarantine. taken: something else is at path. missing: in neither place.

removal.description: What the removal's branch step came to, as recovery.json records it.

action.description: none: the branch is there at its tip. renameBack: kept under keepAs; gets its name back, config included. recreate: deleted and the name free; made again at tip with its recorded config. attach: its name holds another commit and keepAs still has tip; HEAD names keepAs. detach: another worktree uses it, or it moved on; no branch change, HEAD detached at head. null when a problem stops the decision.

occupiedBy.description: The worktree that has the branch — as HEAD, rebasing it, or bisecting from it — when that made the action detach.
